text: Last lesson established why a Client Script can't reach the database directly, and that GlideAjax is the bridge that lets it ask the server instead. This lesson builds the server side of that bridge: the Script Include GlideAjax actually calls.

Any Script Include that's going to be a GlideAjax target must extend a real, built-in ServiceNow class called AbstractAjaxProcessor. You write it with the same Object.extendsObject pattern used throughout the platform, just pointed at AbstractAjaxProcessor instead of a custom base class. Skip this, and GlideAjax simply cannot reach the Script Include at all, no matter what else is configured.

Extending the right class is necessary, but not enough on its own. The Script Include record itself has a Client callable checkbox, and it is unchecked by default. You have to turn it on deliberately. That default-off behavior is a real security setting, keeping ordinary server-side utility code from being accidentally exposed to the browser. And even on a Client callable Script Include, any method whose name starts with an underscore is still never reachable from the client - only plain, public-looking method names are valid targets for a GlideAjax call.

Look at checkDateRange calling an internal helper named with a leading underscore, _hasOverlap. checkDateRange is the public entry point a client can name directly. _hasOverlap can still run - just only from server-side code calling it internally, never as a direct GlideAjax target itself.

Inside a callable method, this.getParameter reads a value the client sent, matched by the exact sysparm_ name used on both sides - sysparm_active, sysparm_start, whatever the client chose. Whatever the method returns becomes the answer that eventually reaches the client's callback function.

So two required things make a Script Include a valid GlideAjax target: extending AbstractAjaxProcessor, and checking Client callable on the record. A third rule, the underscore convention, decides which individual methods on it the client can actually name. Next lesson writes the client script side of this exact bridge.
